title: Longest Subarray With Equal Number of 0s and 1s - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Given an array arr[] of 0s and 1s. Find and return the length of the longest subarray with equal number of 0s and 1s.

Examples: 

Input: arr[] = [1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0]
Output: 6
Explanation: arr[1...6] is the longest subarray with three 0s and three 1s.

Input: arr[] = [0, 0, 1, 1, 0]
Output: 4
Explanation: arr[0...3] or arr[1...4] is the longest subarray with two 0s and two 1s.

Input: arr[] = [0]
Output: 0
Explanation: There is no subarray with an equal number of 0s and 1s.

Try It Yourself

Table of Content

  • [Naive Approach] Nested Loop - O(n ^ 2) Time and O(1) Space
  • [Expected Approach] Hash Map andPrefix Sum - O(n) Time and O(n) Space

[Naive Approach] Nested Loop - O(n ^ 2) Time and O(1) Space

The idea is to generate all possible subarrays and check whether the subarray has equal number of 0s and 1s or not.

Working of Approach:

  • Iterate through every possible starting index s and consider all subarrays starting from that index.
  • Traverse each subarray and treat 0 as -1 and 1 as +1 while maintaining their cumulative sum.
  • If a subarray contains an equal number of 0s and 1s, its converted sum becomes 0.
  • Whenever sum is 0, update res with the maximum length of the valid subarray found so far.
  • After checking all possible subarrays, return res as the maximum length.
C++ 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int maxLen(vector<int> &arr)
{
    int res = 0;

    // Pick a starting point as 's'
    for (int s = 0; s < arr.size(); s++)
    {
        int sum = 0;

        // Consider all subarrays arr[s...e]
        for (int e = s; e < arr.size(); e++)
        {
            sum += (arr[e] == 0) ? -1 : 1;

            // Check if it's a 0-sum subarray
            if (sum == 0)

                // update max size
                res = max(res, e - s + 1);
        }
    }
    return res;
}

int main()
{
    vector<int> arr = {1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0};
    cout << maxLen(arr);
}

[Expected Approach] Hash Map andPrefix Sum - O(n) Time and O(n) Space

The idea is to convert the problem into finding the longest subarray with zero sum.

  • Treat every 0 as -1 and every 1 as +1.
  • Maintain a prefix sum while traversing the array.
  • If the prefix sum is 0 or repeats, update the maximum length.

Let us understand with an example:
Input: arr[] = [1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0]

  • Start with preSum = 0, res = 0, and an empty HashMap.
  • Treat every 0 as -1 and every 1 as +1.
  • At index 0, the element is 1, so preSum = 1. Store 1 -> 0 in the HashMap.
  • At index 1, the element is 0, so preSum = 0. Update res = 2 because the subarray [1, 0] contains an equal number of 0s and 1s.
  • As we continue traversing, whenever a prefix sum repeats, the elements between its previous occurrence and the current index have a sum of 0.
  • At index 6, preSum = 1, which was first seen at index 0. Therefore, the length of the subarray is 6 - 0 = 6, so update res = 6.
  • After traversing the array, the maximum length obtained is 6, corresponding to the subarray [0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0].
C++ 
#include <iostream>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int maxLen(vector<int> &arr)
{
    unordered_map<int, int> mp;

    int preSum = 0;
    int res = 0;

    // Traverse through the given array
    for (int i = 0; i < arr.size(); i++)
    {
        // Add current element to sum
        // if current element is zero, add -1
        preSum += (arr[i] == 0) ? -1 : 1;

        // If prefix sum is 0, the subarray from index 0 to i
        // has an equal number of 0s and 1s
        if (preSum == 0)
            res = i + 1;

        // If this sum is seen before, then update
        // result with maximum
        if (mp.find(preSum) != mp.end())
            res = max(res, i - mp[preSum]);

        // Else put this sum in hash table
        else
            mp[preSum] = i;
    }

    return res;
}

int main()
{
    vector<int> arr = {1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0};

    cout << maxLen(arr) << endl;
    return 0;
}
C 
#include <stdio.h>

#define MAX_SIZE 1000

int maxLen(int arr[], int n)
{
    int firstIndex[2 * MAX_SIZE + 1];

    for (int i = 0; i <= 2 * n; i++)
        firstIndex[i] = -1;

    int preSum = 0;
    int res = 0;
    int offset = n;

    // Traverse through the given array
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
        // Treat 0 as -1 and 1 as +1
        preSum += (arr[i] == 0) ? -1 : 1;

        // If prefix sum is 0, subarray from 0 to i is valid
        if (preSum == 0)
        {
            res = i + 1;
        }

        // If this sum is seen before, update result
        else if (firstIndex[preSum + offset] != -1)
        {
            int len = i - firstIndex[preSum + offset];
            if (len > res)
                res = len;
        }
        else
        {
            // Store the first occurrence of the prefix sum
            firstIndex[preSum + offset] = i;
        }
    }

    return res;
}

int main()
{
    int arr[] = {1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0};
    int n = sizeof(arr) / sizeof(arr[0]);

    printf("%d\n", maxLen(arr, n));

    return 0;
}

import java.util.HashMap;

class GFG {
    static int maxLen(int[] arr)
    {
        HashMap<Integer, Integer> mp = new HashMap<>();

        int preSum = 0;
        int res = 0;

        // Traverse through the given array
        for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {

            // Add current element to sum
            // if current element is zero, add -1
            preSum += (arr[i] == 0) ? -1 : 1;

            // To handle sum = 0 at last index
            if (preSum == 0)
                res = i + 1;

            // If this sum is seen before, then update
            // result with maximum
            if (mp.containsKey(preSum))
                res = Math.max(res, i - mp.get(preSum));

            // Else put this sum in hash table
            else
                mp.put(preSum, i);
        }

        return res;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args)
    {
        int[] arr = { 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0 };

        System.out.println(maxLen(arr));
    }
}
